identity.name: East Turkestan Republic (Second East Turkestan Republic)

land.text: the Ili, Tarbagatay and Altay districts of Xinjiang Province (infobox predecessor: Xinjiang Province, Republic of China)

predecessors.note: Sheng Shicai was removed from Xinjiang in August 1944; the Kuomintang then ran the province. The Cliopatria Republic of China row has no shape between 1943 and 1946 that is checked here.

land.text: the Three Districts, whose National Army was 'incorporated into the People's Liberation Army as the Xinjiang 5th Army Corps' on 20 December 1949

successors.note: The ETR page's own successor is the Ili District Council under the Xinjiang coalition government (June 1946); the Ili Rebellion page says the conflict ended with the Communists' arrival in 1949.

capitals.name: Ghulja (Yining, Kulja)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Ghulja, no coordinates on the page (lon/lat from the gazetteer's Yining).

rulers.name: Elihan Tore
rulers.title: President of the Interim Government
rulers.note: Infobox 'Elihan Tore, President of the Interim Government, 1944-1946'; Hakim Beg Khoja was vice president. The Interim Government became the Ili District Council on 27 June 1946; no ruler list for 1946-1949 is on the pages.

correction.text: the Ili, Tarbagatay and Altay districts at the proclamation of the republic

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins in 1945, but the republic was declared on 12 November 1944 (infobox; the body says 15 November) after the rebels 'assaulted Ghulja on 7 November 1944'. The Three Districts Rebellion 'spread to Altay and Tarbagatay' in October 1944 (page, no day); the 1945 outline of the three districts is used for the year, with the gain event at the proclamation.

273,786 km2 held 1945-1947 (the page gives no area, population 705,168 at the end of 1944). The three districts the page names (Ili with Ghulja, Tarbagatay/Tacheng, Altay) fit the shape; Dihua (Urumqi) 'remained under Kuomintang control' and the Ili forces 'almost succeeded in reaching Urumqi' (Ili Rebellion page) without holding it; the push to Kashgar, Kargilik and Yarkand failed. The shape does not include the Manas front of September 1945, which is the contest zone in the ledger.

Same outline minus three cells (759 km2) at 87.5-90.0E 45.3-45.9N, noise. The coalition government collapsed on 12 August 1947 and 'governance resumed in former ETR territories' (infobox); in September 1947 Osman Batur's Kazakhs, with Chinese support, 'seized most of its towns' in the Ashan zone; the pages do not say who held the zone afterwards, so the shape stands.

Same outline as 1945 (the three cells return). The National Army was incorporated into the PLA on 20 December 1949; the Ili leaders agreed to join the PRC on 3 September 1949 (Ili Rebellion page) and the PLA entered Xinjiang on 12 October.

region.text: Ghulja (Yining, Kulja) and the Ili valley

ledger.note: 12 November 1944: the East Turkestan Republic is proclaimed at Ghulja. Infobox 'Established: 12 November 1944' (the body gives 15 November): 'The rebels assaulted Ghulja on 7 November 1944'; the Kuomintang's last posts there fell on 13 November. The republic is described as a satellite state of the Soviet Union.

October-November 1944: the rising spreads to the Tarbagatay and Altay districts. 'The Three Districts Rebellion broke out south of Ghulja and spread to Altay and Tarbagatay'; the page names Ili, Tarbagatay (Tacheng) and Altay as the three districts but dates neither city's fall.

region.text: the Manasi River front north of Dihua: Shihezi, Jinghe and Dushanzi

ledger.note: September 1945: the Ili National Army reaches the Manas River. 'ETR forces fought near Shihezi, Jinghe, and Dushanzi, capturing KMT bases and oil fields. By September, ETR forces were on the Manasi River north of Dihua.' The Soviet-Chinese treaty of August 1945 had ended overt Soviet support.

2 January 1946: a preliminary peace is signed at Dihua. 'A preliminary peace agreement was signed in Dihua under Soviet mediation'; the peace agreement of 6 June 1946 'reduced the National Army to 11,000-12,000 troops, confined to the Three Districts'.

27 June 1946: the republic becomes the Ili District Council. 'Resolution 324 transformed the interim government into the Ili District Council and dissolved the ETR'; the Coalition Government of Xinjiang Province was set up at Dihua on 1 July 1946. The Ili Rebellion page puts the ceasefire and coalition on 26 June. The council keeps the Three Districts and the National Army (the Ili Rebellion page says nothing of a separate administration, so the continuity is Cliopatria's shape).

12 August 1947: the Xinjiang coalition collapses. The Ili Rebellion infobox dates the collapse to 12 August 1947 and says 'governance resumed in former ETR territories'; in June 1947 Mongol and Soviet forces had attacked the Kazakhs and in September Osman Batur's Kazakhs seized towns in the Ashan zone. The page does not name who governed the Three Districts afterwards.

region.text: the Three Districts of Ili, Tarbagatay and Altay

ledger.note: 20 December 1949: the Three Districts' National Army joins the People's Liberation Army. 'The National Army was incorporated into the People's Liberation Army as the Xinjiang 5th Army Corps.' The page does not call it the end of a state; the Ili Rebellion page has the leaders agreeing to join the PRC on 3 September 1949 and the PLA entering Xinjiang on 12 October.

wars.name: Ili Rebellion (Three Districts Revolution)

zones.text: the Manasi River front north of Dihua
Ghulja (Yining, Kulja) and the Ili valley

wars.outcome: Ghulja stormed 7-13 November 1944; the Ili forces took the oil fields at Dushanzi in September 1945 and stood on the Manasi River; Soviet-mediated talks opened on 14 October 1945, a preliminary peace was signed on 2 January 1946 and the agreement of June 1946 confined the National Army to the Three Districts.
wars.note: The Ili Rebellion infobox ends the conflict on 26 June 1946, the text on the Communists' arrival in 1949 (conflicting).

wars.name: Osman Batur's offensive in the Ashan zone

zones.text: the Ashan zone (read as the Altay district)

wars.outcome: In September 1947, in a Chinese-supported offensive, Osman Batur's Kazakhs 'defeated and killed ETR forces in the Ashan zone and seized most of its towns'; the pages do not say how the zone was held afterwards.
wars.note: Reading Ashan as Altay is the researcher's; the page does not equate them, so no contest event is entered.

certainty.note: No boundary line is described on either page; the Three Districts are administrative units and the Manasi River front of September 1945 was a battle line.

notes: Cliopatria's shape covers the Three Districts for 1945-1949 while the ETR page ends the republic on 27 June 1946 (Resolution 324, Ili District Council in the Xinjiang coalition government) and the Ili Rebellion page ends the conflict in 1949; the dossier follows Cliopatria's continuity (end December 1949, with rename events in June 1946 and August 1947) and a reviewer may prefer an end in June 1946 with the later years drawn as a Republic of China autonomous district. The Cliopatria row 'East Turkestan' (1463-1474) shares Wikidata Q840601 with this row but is a different state (the Moghul-era Kashgaria polity, dossier east-turkestan); the shared id is a Cliopatria mistake. Relations other dossiers should carry: the Soviet Union backed the republic as a satellite (arms, advisers, 'direct military support in 1944-45', ended by the August 1945 treaty; union-of-soviet-socialist-republics vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart east-turkestan-republic); the Republic of China (ea-08) gains the Three Districts back in June 1946 as the Ili District Council and loses them again in August 1947 on the pages' reading. The Sariqol (Tashkurgan) rebellion of 19 August 1945 in southern Xinjiang was separate and is not entered. Not settled: the dates of the fall of Tacheng and Altay, the Ashan zone (read as Altay), the uncertainty over the two dates of the proclamation (12 or 15 November 1944), the Hami and Kashgar fronts, the native (Uyghur) name (not on the pages), and what happened between August 1947 and December 1949. Names Yining, Tacheng, Altay and Shihezi resolve in the gazetteer.
